UNSUPPORTED means absent or contradicted; AMBIGUOUS means entailment remains uncertain.
Never infer satisfaction from keyword presence, a future intention instead of action, wrong actors, negation, hearsay, or an invented clue. Cite exact_text verbatim.

STORY_STATE_KNOWLEDGE requires the subject's exact /characters/.../knowledge/N pointer and evidence_subject equal to that knowledge entry; still cite its actual use in prose.
No invented world rules, clues or unestablished lore can support an event.
ALL_PREDICATES is the entire satisfaction rule. Do not add unstated obligations.
Return residual as a spineforge-relay.semantic-guard.v1 report. Audit residual continuity, causality, character identity canon, epistemic leaks, forbidden facts, state/exit obligations and meaning ambiguities.
PASS requires no blockers. The local evaluator independently checks coverage, attribution, provenance and anchors.

sight"},"target_words_min":200,"target_words_max":320,"max_rewrites":1},"relevant_character_canon":{"Ekin":{"age":12,"identity":"girl","pronouns":["she","her"]},"Duru":{"age":12,"identity":"girl","pronouns":["she","her"]}},"candidate_prose":"The sea dragon swept through the open lighthouse door, its wet wings nearly brushing the walls. Ekin pressed herself against the dry stone as it crossed the daylight spilling through the upper windows.

The brass compass hung from the dragon’s jaws.

“Grandfather’s compass,” Ekin whispered.

The dragon lowered its head over a rough nest beside the wall and placed the compass among the twisted reeds. Sunlight flashed on its scratched lid. Ekin saw it clearly, only a few quick steps away.

She started forward.

“Wait,” Duru said.

A small shape stirred inside the nest. Duru noticed it first and pointed. Ekin followed his finger.

A sea dragon hatchling, no larger than a cat, pushed its head above the reeds. Its little wings opened and fluttered, but they could not lift it. Unhurt, it clambered beside the compass.

The mother dragon swung around. She planted herself between the children and the nest, wings half spread, blocking the approach. Ekin stopped as the dragon’s claws scraped the floor.

At the other side of the upper room, a narrow turning stair led down toward the lower maintenance room. Ekin and Duru remained on the upper-room floor and looked down its tight curve. Through the stair opening, they could both see a fixed iron grate in the sea-facing wall below. Gray light and harbor water gleamed between its bars.

Duru glanced from the stair to the mother dragon. “Don’t rush her.”

Ekin’s hands curled into fists inside her jacket pockets. He was right that the nest was blocked. She could see that perfectly well.

But she could also see the compass shining beside the hatchling.

“It’s right there,” she said, sharper than she meant. “I’m not leaving it.”","deterministic_findings":[]}
